message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
You can use either the **gcloud CLI** (recommended for quick testing) or the **REST API** if you prefer to embed it in your own tooling.

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** must be enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * You need a service account with the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role (or equivalent) if you’re calling the REST API.  
> * The **NVIDIA GPU driver** will be installed automatically by the image’s startup script.  

---

## 1. Using the gcloud CLI

```bash
# Variables – change these to suit your environment
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator=type="$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-standard \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### Optional: Startup script (`startup.sh`)

The Ubuntu 20.04 image includes a startup script that installs the NVIDIA driver automatically.  
If you want to customize it, create a `startup.sh` file in the same directory:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA driver (auto‑install via the image)
# You can add additional packages here
apt-get update
apt-get install -y build-essential
```

Make sure the script is executable:

```bash
chmod +x startup.sh
```

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON payload)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a CI/CD pipeline), use the following JSON body.  
Replace the placeholder values (`YOUR_PROJECT_ID`, `YOUR_ZONE`, etc.) with your actual data.

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100
      },
      "diskType": "zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-standard"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\n# Custom startup commands here\n"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### REST API call

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/YOUR_ZONE/instances"
```

> Replace `@instance.json` with the path to the JSON file containing the payload above.

---

## 3. Verify the instance

After creation, you can check that the GPU is attached and the driver is installed:

```bash
# SSH into the instance
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone us-central1-a

# Inside the VM
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

---

### Quick checklist

| Step | Command / Action |
|------|------------------|
| Enable Compute Engine API | `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` |
| Create instance (CLI) | `gcloud compute instances create ...` |
| Or create instance (REST) | `curl -X POST ...` |
| Verify GPU | `nvidia-smi` inside the VM |

That’s it! You now have a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU. Happy computing!
